notes.title: Hyperbrawl’s Revolutionary Sound Design
notes.notes:
Music and Audio are what help create immersion within video games, without sound there is no player experience. 

For HyperBrawl we wanted to push the boundaries of what was possible with music and audio design and through the use of the brand new machine-learning audio design technology Omnio we were able to dynamically add spatial information to audio in real-time giving audiences the physical sensation of immersion in a way that has never been put into working practice in a video game before.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/67e57ce58eba5448b0f1da8b385e696bb43af158.jpg[/img]

Throughout the development of HyperBrawl Tournament our team worked alongside the team at Omnio and legendary music composer Steve Levine to become the first ever video game in history to use this revolutionary music industry and nightlife technology within interactive media.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/a7311680fe0c9f62bd3f336ddf940499dd7394d8.png[/img]

Using Omnio, we were able to take the audio design of HyperBrawl Tournament and enable players to feel audio and experience music the way it sounded when originally recorded in a way that has never been done in video game development before and display what is possible with game audio in the modern era.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/252cde59c017dafe28c6ff13bd963757591e868a.png[/img]

To convert the tracks of HyperBrawl Tournament our team and Steve Levine passed each of the games audio tracks through a black box provided by Steve containing a unique chipset that utalized a special algorithm to remaster the sound for our team and create audio that is both reactive to the players actions in the game world but also matches the audio to what is happening in the present moment.


To learn more about the music and sound production of HyperBrawl check out our official documentary The Music of HyperBrawl Tournament.

[previewyoutube=INEK7Bl0egM;full][/previewyoutube]

We have more news coming for HyperBrawl Tournament on Steam in the near future so make sure to keep an eye on our social channels and we look forward to seeing you in the Brawl.

notes.title: Play the HyperBrawl Tournament Demo Now!

[h1]Play the HyperBrawl Tournament demo before launch on 20th October![/h1]

Before our official launch of HyperBrawl Tournament on the 20th October, we're giving you an opportunity to get a hands on look at the game during the Steam Game Festival: Autumn Edition.

This demo contains tonnes of new features from the full game to whet your brawling appetite:
[list]
[*] Three arenas to battle it out in - Temple of Entropy, The Foundry and Court of Azdritch. 
[*] Four playable heroes - Shade, Tristan, Toro and Go-Zen. 
[*] Five powerful weapons to wield (including some fancy new ones!) - Sentry Shield, Cyclone Sword, Grapple Gun, Boost Bomber and Turbo Thruster.
[/list]

There are four game modes to compete in - 
[list]
[*] ARCADE - Jump into instant local multiplayer or single player matches for 1-4 players, earn XP and level up.
[*] BLITZ – Compete online with players across the world for the ultimate accolade, becoming the ‘The HyperBrawl Champion’, the longer the win streak, the greater the rewards
[*] PRIVATE MATCH – Create or join a match online to prove yourself amongst your friends and reign over them with your superior HyperBrawl skills.
[*] THE TRIALS – Enter the tutorial and practice your skills before entering the arena.
[/list]

To start your journey into the HyperVerse and to give you a headstart over your opponents in the race to the top of the global leaderboards, we have created a couple of introductory videos to two of the games key features:

[h2]HyperCurve[/h2]

The HyperCurve is one of the game’s core mechanics, and it lets you control the ball mid-air. Using this ability, every match becomes considerably less predictable – and allows you to score a goal from pretty much anywhere in the arena – especially if your opponent didn’t see it coming. Mastering this gravity-defying ability will take your game to the next level!

[previewyoutube=V_Pb8BzDn0w;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]HyperForce[/h2]

For the times where the match may not be going your way, you can channel the HyperForce, which gives your heroes super-human powers and the ability to launch their rivals out of the arena to help ensure victory!

[previewyoutube=duC3B_is2SM;full][/previewyoutube]

This has been a three year labour of love for our team and we are so glad to bring you an exclusive taste of the game before our launch on the 20th October. Thank you for all of your support you have given us on this journey, it has meant the world to us! 

We really hope you enjoy the HyperBrawl Demo experience. notes.title: Behind the Brawl #5: Hero Design & Development
notes.notes:
Hi brawlers!

[b]K. A.[/b] here, [b]Community Manager[/b] for HyperBrawl Tournament. I'm back with another [b]Behind the Brawl[/b] development blog and this time I've sat down with our [b]Game Designer[/b], [b]Scott[/b], to look at HyperBrawl's three different hero classes - and why they're important to gameplay. Let's jump in!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/b7ae66e44c98f9ba7f623d0b7766ac650617c085.png[/img]

[h1]Hero classes - what are they?[/h1]
The heroes of HyperBrawl come in three different types; Swift, Tank and Core. These classes offer slightly different play styles and benefits, giving players more strategy and diversity in their gameplay. Here's the quick rundown:
[list][*][b]Swift[/b] heroes are faster and more agile, but can't deal or take as much damage. They're good for getting around the arena quickly, but less capable in a brawl.
[*][b]Tank[/b] heroes are very strong and have more health, but are slower than other hero types. They can be great in a brawl or at defending the goal area.
[*][b]Core[/b] heroes are jack of all trades. They're somewhere in between the other two types, which makes them good at everything, without excelling at anything.[/list]
Ultimately it's important to note that any hero can be used for any job; it all depends on your play style and what your opponent is bringing to the brawl.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/dc369d60750450f997bb0ee6b40a31358b7cc7f3.png[/img]

[h1]Settling on three classes[/h1]
In the very early days of development, each hero was much more unique and had their own abilities, though this quickly became very difficult to balance. Another concern was how confusing it became to play, when you would suddenly need hours of practice to learn the ins and outs of each character. Being able to just pick up the controller and play was always important to us, so the system needed simplification.

With a class system, the game became much easier to both balance and understand. Settling on a few classes allowed us to be able to fall back on class rule sets to help balance the game, while making the game in a way that most players would be able to get into more easily, simply because it's so common in other games and genres already.

Turning the unique heroes into class-based archetypes was actually what introduced the weapons we have today. Each hero was originally conceived to have their own unique abilities/weapons, but the class system allowed us to separate the heroes from the weapons, which now means that any hero can use any weapon. This has allowed for considerably more flexibility in each player's play style - and allows you to really play the game any way you want, with whatever hero and weapon combination you prefer.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/62b7fdc35ea830341b4a1ed947cbca86ec86ba12.jpg[/img]

[h1]Balancing each hero[/h1]
Balancing became a lot easier once we decided on the hero classes and their pre-defined rule sets. We did a lot of testing in the early stages of development, that allowed us to lock down each class' behaviour quite quickly. Now when we add a new hero to the roster, we assign them a class and that immediately gives us a specific framework to work from. This allows us to still be creative and make them unique within their given class, without risking their overall balance getting out of hand.

As each hero has their own unique stats, however, there is still some tweaking that can be done on a hero-by-hero basis - and as we see players experiment and provide us with feedback, changes can quite easily be made over time as needed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/33f89165faa30c1ff5fb235302c63cafee1380f7.png[/img]

[h1]Advice for new players[/h1]
Experimentation is the key. The team's done their best to ensure, that HyperBrawl doesn't have a "best loadout"; it all depends on your play style. Maybe you like the Tank characters for their added health or ability to goal keep, or maybe you prefer a Swift class for their ability to out-run the slower heroes, opening up new opportunities in the arena. 

Generally, we'd advise that you try all three classes and the various weapon combinations to find what works for you. Changing up your weapon can completely change how you play a specific hero or class too; you may normally want to keep your distance with a Swift character due to their low health, but equipping them with the Slam Hammer and getting up close and personal for a devastating attack can be effective too. Experiment and have fun - and let us know your favourites!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/e2917da9f90bd1da62ba1b361c30c540b9149232.jpg[/img]

[h1]Want to know more?[/h1]
That's it for this Behind the Brawl dev blog. We've now done five of these and are always keen to know what you would like us to talk about in the future. Whether you're curious about HyperBrawl's gameplay or development, ask away and we'll answer best we can!

For the latest news as well as the occasional tips and tricks, be sure to follow us on [url=http://www.twitter.com/hyperbrawl]Twitter[/url] or join us on [url=http://discord.gg/hyperbrawl]Discord[/url]. [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/90895289d7252e5acd42d553e5692d6ec58c0cc1.png[/img]
Hi brawlers!

Welcome to Behind the Brawl #4, in which we'll be looking back at our most recent Steam beta. The May 2020 beta ended just a few days ago, and we've spent the last couple of days combing through all the awesome feedback that we've received from all of you. This once again included both things we've nailed so far, as well as things we need to make even better. First, let's take a look at some of the key statistics from the beta.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/16a99eb12b8a44dc0e724a0cc0abcb395537722a.jpg[/img]

Now let's dive into some of the key takeaways from the beta itself!

[h1]The Pros[/h1][list]
[*][b]Players had a great time![/b] Just like with the previous beta, everyone keeps telling us that the overall HyperBrawl experience is really fun, which is obviously essential for us!
[*][b]Our competitions ensured, well, competition![/b] We ran a number of competitions during the beta and particularly the one that rewarded the top 3 players on our Most Online Wins leaderboard created quite a lot of heated competition! [url=https://www.hyperbrawl.com/news-and-updates/beta-competitions]Find all the winners here![/url]
[*][b]The new selection of heroes and weapons created new player strategies![/b] With all weapons from the previous beta swapped out, players used a lot of new strategies, many of which were new to us. It'll be interesting to see which strategies prevail once players have access to everything at launch!
[*][b]We had a ton of new players enter the arena![/b] It was awesome seeing so many new brawlers enter the arena and a lot of that was thanks to all of you bringing in family and friends alike. Spreading the word is key to an active player base at launch, so we really appreciate everyone's help with this!
[*][b]The player skill cap keeps going up![/b] We keep being blown away by how good players are getting and we've already got several players in the community that bring both a challenge - and a beatdown - to the developers in the arena! [i][b]Practice intensifies![/b][/i][/list]

[i][b]With great power comes great... double KO goals![/b][/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/b2024379e9f820d14d9f93fbbd2c417c877bbd33.gif[/img]

[h1]The cons[/h1][list]
[*][b]We still have bugs to squash![/b] Our last two Steam betas have both been running on several months old code, which means a lot of reported issues have already been fixed in the full version of the game. That being said, thanks to your detailed feedback - and even videos showing the exact issues - we've been able to identify additional things that need addressing. Some of these are bugs and others are gameplay adjustments that we're now investigating further. Thanks for your help on this!
[*][b]The Turbo Thruster became a must-use weapon![/b] While this might not sound like an issue, we've seen the Turbo Thruster used in new ways, which means that we'll now be looking at whether it needs any adjustments for the full game, as all weapons have obviously been balanced with the full roster of weapons in mind, and not specifically for this beta where only three weapons were available.[/list]

[i][b]Ricochet with great care, brawlers...[/b][/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/b3fe7e1cead212fca7f2c0dc3ae8315527a3c6e1.gif[/img]

[h1]So, now what?[/h1]
While we get ever closer to the game's full lunch later this year, we're currently working on additional opportunities for everyone to get in on the action, and show their friends who's boss. One of these opportunities is the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/sale/gamefestival]Steam Game Festival[/url] taking place 16th-22nd June. We'll have more details on this soon, so keep an eye on our channels - like [url=http://www.twitter.com/hyperbrawl]Twitter[/url] and [url=http://discord.gg/hyperbrawl]Discord[/url] - for more information!

For now, if you've enjoyed what you've seen (and hopefully played) so far, make sure to add HyperBrawl to your Steam wishlist - it [b]really[/b] helps more players discover the game. The more players, the more fun competition we'll all have at launch and beyond!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/591760/HyperBrawl_Tournament/

See you in the arena!

notes.title: Behind the Brawl #3 - How we design HyperBrawl arenas
notes.notes:
Hi brawlers

K. A. here, Community Manager at Milky Tea. It's time for another [b]Behind the Brawl[/b] development blog and this time I've asked Luke, artist at Milky Tea, to take us through the process of designing unique arenas for [b]HyperBrawl Tournament[/b]. Curious about the considerations going into it? And wondering why we're not creating star-shaped arenas? Read on below!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/21745fa268745e328d2ceff3ae61c050784a2e18.jpg[/img]

[h2]Designing arenas for HyperBrawl Tournament[/h2]
Hey everyone, Luke here. I'll be explaining what goes into designing our arenas, and a little about the exciting worlds our arenas take place in. In this edition of Behind the Brawl I'll discuss the shapes of our arenas, their unique mechanics and some of the design decisions that we have to tackle along the way.

Our arena shapes and mechanics dictate your strategies, they influence your play styles and they are vital to our very important video game development Fun Calculations™ to ensure you’re having the most Fun™ you can possibly have!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/a8134e5c06ceba243a97228d54c76ac380a02fb3.gif[/img]

[h2]Where it all began[/h2]
When we first began development, our focus was primarily on the gameplay itself and the first playable HyperBrawl arena was nothing but a rectangle with two goals on either end.

We had these instantly enjoyable character controls and exciting abilities such as Weapons, Dive Rolls and HyperCurve; the power to bend the ball around the pitch. But no matter what mechanics we injected into the characters, every game was a case of ‘run to the ball first, shoot, score, repeat’. There wasn’t much incentive for the players to develop strategies and attempt to out-play their opponents.

By the simple act of adding a static box to the middle of the arena, we instantly improved the variety of gameplay potential and skill based purely on how we approached manoeuvring around this box and opponents, who were also trying to use it to their advantage. It also made abilities like HyperCurve much more relevant and increased the skill level exponentially.

Expanding on that idea, that simple box evolved into mechanics such as constantly shifting pillars, rotating floors and much, much more, further improving gameplay and strategy variety.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/7f8d92e921882912f414c8b2ef803935de96d7c2.gif[/img]

[h1]Considerations in creating a new arena[/h1]
[h2]Our favourite shapes[/h2]
After our first arena we also began to experiment with new arena shape designs, recognising that there was huge potential for gameplay variety purely by changing the orientation of the surrounding walls.

Based on our design experiences with trying out different ideas over the years, there are a couple of rules that we keep into consideration when designing a new one. So far, our roster of arena shapes has been perfected down to these 4 styles:
[list][*] Rectangle
[*] Long Rectangle
[*] Circle
[*] Octagon[/list]
These are the shapes that we feel give us the appropriate playspace we need to still be able to fill the arena with interesting mechanics, and have enough room for the players to move around and find their own playstyles. Combined with the unique mechanics each and every arena is a different experience!

[h2]What about a... rhombus?[/h2]
We have of course prototyped other shapes throughout HyperBrawl’s development, but there are a lot of things we had to take into consideration, including:
[list]
[*] Symmetry, so both players have equal playspace and neither has an advantage over the other.
[*] Readability. Arenas need to be simple and instantly understandable, especially from the point-of-view of our fixed camera positions.
[*] Interactable, as in, what shapes give the player the ability to use the wall angles to their advantage by ricocheting the ball or other potential strategies.
[/list]
With more arenas to come, we will be continuously experimenting with different kinds of shapes and listening constantly to our community to hear their ideas on new shapes to try! But no rhombuses.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/f14435776f7041b39acea275e3932443d98bd1f1.jpg[/img]

[h2]Dynamic mechanics[/h2]
As with the shapes, over the course of development we began to figure out the rules of what we feel make a fun and fair HyperBrawl arena mechanic. During the days where there were no wrong ideas, we came up with a lot of very wrong ideas, which included mechanics/obstacles that would KO or harm the players. We quickly realised such mechanics added an unnecessary amount of frustration, and players were much more receptive to obstacles that simply changed how they manoeuvred the arena and their opponents, as well as challenge their HyperCurve skills.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/6432b87becd995aa58c10511c22ae1c65c67d7d4.jpg[/img]

There were also other mechanics that did not harm the player, and were for all intents and purposes Fun™, such as an arena filled with bouncy trampolines that projected the player upwards into the air! However after the novelty of being tossed into the sky had worn off, it just became annoying when a player was about to score a goal only to accidentally go flying and ruining their flow or strategy.

So to summarise, the connection between our shapes and mechanics, is that we never want to distract from the objective which is scoring jaw-dropping goals and outplaying your opponents. The arena as a whole should be instantly readable, with just enough complexity and variety that a more advanced player can take advantage of it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/96eac06df562b60b83f5a39e26acd84d82fc8acf.gif[/img]

[h2]New worlds[/h2]
In a universe that literally spans all of time and space, there is no limit to the kinds of worlds that our arenas can exist in, and this can be as daunting as it is liberating. When you have infinite possibilities to pick from, it can be difficult to choose the one that fits your existing universe the best.  Luckily all of our creations inspire each other, so if we have an awesome character in the works that has yet to be given a home, or there is a storytelling hint in one of our existing arenas or character backstories that literally inspires whole new worlds and characters into creation, that just helps us construct arenas that can exist in a universe of limitless potential, but still feel very important to the world of HyperBrawl.

The magic to making a HyperBrawl arena, comes when we mix and match our catalogue of arena shapes that we know work best, mechanics that give the player an exciting blend of challenge and opportunity, and wrap it up in an inspired and unique environment that cements the arena within the HyperBrawl universe, as well as just looking amazingly awesome to boot!

[h1]That's a wrap![/h1]
That's it for our third dev blog for HyperBrawl Tournament. Thanks to Luke for educating us on the wonderful world of arenas!

As always, do let us know what you thought of the blog, as well as which other topics you'd like for us to cover in the future. 

Outside of Steam we'd love to talk to you on [url=https://twitter.com/HyperBrawl]Twitter[/url] or [url=http://discord.gg/hyperbrawl]Discord[/url], which are two great places to stay up-to-date on everything HyperBrawl. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/591760/HyperBrawl_Tournament/
Finally, be sure to wishlist HyperBrawl Tournament right here on Steam if you're looking forward to launch later this year.

Anyway, thanks for reading. See you in the arena!

notes.title: Behind the Brawl #2 - How we create HyperBrawl weapons
notes.notes:
Hi brawlers

I'm K. A., the Community Manager here at Milky Tea and I'd like to welcome you to our second [b]Behind the Brawl[/b] dev blog. For this one I've sat down with Scott, one of our designers, and asked him to take us through the development of a weapon in HyperBrawl. There are quite a few things to consider during this process, so fair warning; this post is quite long. Grab your popcorn and let's jump in!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/7aacce50391f38e06d4d02e3f5bb75bf79302047.png[/img]

[h1]Weapons in HyperBrawl[/h1]
One of the main features in HyperBrawl is the weapons. Alongside selecting a hero, which offer their own attributes, players can select a weapon to take into the match with them. Each weapon gives players a unique ability to assist them in the game, so picking the right weapon for the right situation can make all the difference.

When it comes to designing a new weapon for HyperBrawl, we have figured out a nice process for making sure weapons are as fun, exciting, and as balanced as they can be. 

Our first step, as with most design work, is to brainstorm a list of weapons which we think would be cool. This first stage is always very open, creative, and at this point no idea is a bad idea. From this initial brainstorm we will have several ideas which we will further discuss, and rate based on numerous considerations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/c85ec30538e9b92dd4cc1a5c29948a9b44d13d56.png[/img]

[h1]Considerations in creating a new weapon[/h1]
[h2]Does it make sense in the game world?[/h2]
Luckily with HyperBrawl, the game world is incredibly diverse and spans an entire universe, with tons of different cultural references. Because of this, most weapon types could potentially make sense in the game.

That being said, all the weapons in the game share a similar aesthetic style. This is to make weapons more immediately recognisable to the player. We experimented with more bespoke styles earlier on in the development, but we found it ended up being much more confusing for players. 

Before we begin putting the weapon in the game, we concept up ideas for how the weapon will look in the game world, both up close, and from the player’s camera. If we find the weapon isn’t recognisable or often gets lost in the action, we will look at redesigning the visuals, or potentially scrapping the idea entirely.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/2b07461e062f04d113f9d178b289e0856b4176a1.png[/img]

[h2]Does it work with existing mechanics in the game?[/h2]
In HyperBrawl, all weapons have a single use (e.g. the player presses a single button to use the weapon). Therefore, we wouldn’t want to introduce a weapon which requires holding down two buttons for example.

We need to ensure new weapons don’t disrupt the main pillars of the game’s design or require us to change how other mechanics work drastically. Ideally the implementation of one weapon doesn't require us to change every other weapon to keep the weapon balance in place.

[h2]Will the weapon be easy to balance?[/h2]
Whenever we prototype a new weapon, chances are that it will be overpowered or underpowered in some way. This is okay though, because most of the time it can be resolved quite easily. That being said, if we test a weapon for a long time, and it continues to be unbalanced it may be easier to just remove the weapon from the game. Unfortunately not everything is as good in practice as it may have been on paper.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/f507a79605513e132630f2591932cad03d4152c3.gif[/img]

[h2]Might there be any online issues?[/h2]
As HyperBrawl is a fast-paced competitive online multiplayer game, we need to ensure any new weapons we create are reasonably simple to network, and we need to be sure it won’t create any issues in an online match.

As an example, we had a bug with the [b]Mine Mortar[/b] early in development, where the targeted player couldn't see the mine, and on their screen they just randomly blew up by something they couldn't see. It wasn’t the most balanced experience to say the least. Fortunately we were able to quickly identify and fix the issue, so now you can blow up your opponents without worry!

[h2]Is the weapon fun for both the user and the victim?[/h2]
It’s obvious that we want weapons to be fun for the player who is using them – they should feel exciting and rewarding when used, especially when used successfully. At the same time, it should be quite fun for the victim of the weapon. This may sound strange, but the player who is targeted by the weapon should have the ability to counter it, and if they do get hit by it, it shouldn’t frustrate them too much.

One example of this is an old weapon which used to be in the game; [b]The Reverse Potion[/b]. This weapon was a grenade which reversed a player's controls if they were hit by it. This was an interesting idea on paper, and it was very useful for the player using it. Unfortunately it was extremely frustrating for the player who was hit by it, as their character was essentially uncontrollable for about 10 seconds - which is about three times as long as a knock out. During early tests we found that matches using the Reverse Potion left players feeling frustrated and annoyed, so it was ultimately removed. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/f289ae3217932f88cb6a901d7f3864d8c3ae612a.gif[/img]

[h1]Balancing our weapons[/h1]
We recently ran a closed PC beta for HyperBrawl Tournament and received some great feedback from our players. Thanks again for that!
 
One reason for our beta tests is to spot issues with balancing we may otherwise not notice. Once many players enter the arena, new strategies and playstyles emerge naturally which is awesome to see, but occasionally these can cause balance issues and become frustrating for other players.
 
One of these issues was the [b]Sentry Shield[/b], which turned out to be quite overpowered. Let's look at weapon balancing with a focus on this particular weapon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/ed0a4da1c61d01d39baf2ee4a5c2fd07d9bc0b23.gif[/img]

[h2]How the Sentry Shield currently works[/h2]
Here’s how the Sentry Shield worked in the most recent closed beta:[list]
[*]It is placed directly in front of the player and spawns a large barrier.
[*]When the barrier is hit by the ball or a player, it’s reduced 50% in size. If it is hit once more, it will disappear.
[*]If placed correctly players can block two shots with the shield.[/list]

[h2]The problem[/h2]
During the closed beta, more and more players would make sure to equip the shield on at least one hero, and whenever it was ready to use (around every 20 seconds) they would place it directly in their own goal. This eventually became the meta during the beta, and a ton of players always had a shield in their goal for most of their matches.
 
This frustrated opponents as it felt like quite a cheap tactic, and by the time two shots were blocked, the player would soon be able to place another shield. It took a lot of the intensity out of the game, which obviously wasn’t great.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/9ec7afa290e7ae3018ba3b7b1b9689086d8255c7.gif[/img]

[h2]The potential solutions[/h2]
There are several options we’re considering in terms of balancing the Sentry Shield:[list]
[*][b]Increase the cooldown timer[/b]. A simple fix; longer cooldowns = less shields uptime. However, this probably wouldn’t solve the main issue, which is being able to place the shield in your goal to stop players from scoring so often.
[*][b]Stop the shield from being placed in the goal area[/b]. This is difficult because of the visual feedback that may be required. If a player tries to place the shield in the goal area, what happens? This would be a great fix, because it would create more interesting situations where players wouldn’t be able to directly block the goal, but still cause their opponent to shoot from different angles and use HyperCurve.
[*][b]Reduce the shield’s “health” by 50%[/b]. Players can still make that one key block if they use the shield well.
[*][b]Add a set duration to the Shield[/b]. The shield could be used in the same way, but only for a limited time, making players much more cautious about when and how they use it.[/list]

[h2]So, now what?[/h2]
With all these options in mind, we need to ensure the shield remains balanced in comparison to the rest of the weapons in the game.[list]
[*]It needs to remain fun to use, while providing interesting and useful strategical opportunities.
[*]It should remain powerful and useful for players, but opponents should always have a way to counter the weapon.
[*]Weapons should be balanced enough that none feel completely essential to each match as this will make gameplay less diverse and interesting.[/list]
We’re testing the options above, and possibly some more in-game currently. We’re hoping to get a much-improved shield in the game for future beta tests.

[h1]That's all, folks![/h1]
That's it for our second dev blog for HyperBrawl Tournament. Thanks to Scott for giving us some valuable time and thank you, dear reader, for making it this far! You're still here, right?

Anyway, please do let us know your thoughts, and if there are any particular aspects of game development you would like to learn more about. We've got a lot more dev blogs planned, so please do keep providing us with feedback and suggestions for what you'd like to see next.

Also, if you've got any questions or thoughts on any of the above, do let us know. Do you perhaps have other suggestions for how we could adjust the shield? Or a cool idea for an awesome weapon we could add in the future? Let us know!

As always, we'd love to talk to you on [url=https://twitter.com/HyperBrawl]Twitter[/url] or [url=http://discord.gg/hyperbrawl]Discord[/url], which are two great places to stay up-to-date on everything HyperBrawl. Hope to see you there!

See you in the arena!

notes.title: Behind the Brawl #1: Beta takeaways and next steps
notes.notes:
HI brawlers

Welcome to the very first [b]Behind the Brawl[/b], a development series where we'll be looking at challenges, considerations and behind-the-scenes of how HyperBrawl Tournament is being developed. This first part will specifically look at what we learned during the most recent beta - and where we go from here.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/b3a084a44ceed94167dc8a031b8f5912ac5419a6.png[/img]

We recently ran our first PC beta of 2020 right here on Steam and as we’re currently working on the next one, we wanted to take a moment to reflect on the key takeaways and look at where we’re going from here.

We received a ton of feedback from everyone during the beta, which highlighted both known and new issues, as well as general things for us to consider going forward in development. Let’s dive into some of these!

[h1]The pros[/h1]
[list][*][b]Players told us they had a great time during the beta[/b] and made sure to inform us of specific instances where the game needs adjustments. We’re working on those right now!
[*][b]Our multiplayer technology performed really well[/b] with minimal lag during online matches. Score!
[*][b]Players brawled with both controllers and keyboard/mouse[/b]. While we’ve always recommended playing with controllers, it was great to see that both options are viable in the arena – and that the player skill level was super high on both!
[*][b]A ton of players were really good[/b]! Almost [b]too good[/b], though, as even the developers lost countless matches. We need to practice!
[*][b]A lot of you put in the work and hit the level cap![/b] Maybe we should increase the cap for the next beta...
[*][b]Many players mastered the HyperCurve[/b] while others never used it at all. We need to show everyone just how awesome the HyperCurve really is! Case in point:[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/3bb593eb59bf8a9eaa86e89230e87c4a058646f9.gif[/img]
[i]Thanks to [url=https://mixer.com/oldarobot]Olda Robot[/url] for the [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u9KaqG0F5T4]original clip[/url][/i]

Make sure to HyperCurve responsibly though, or this might happen...
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/f4cc03e3f520c2d04c9eff0a03f6f6c928e6e12e.gif[/img]
[i]Thanks to [url=https://mixer.com/oldarobot]Olda Robot[/url] for the karma-filled [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eU3KABndx4o]original clip[/url][/i]

[h1]The cons[/h1][list]
[*][b]A number of things didn’t quite work as intended[/b], and while much of this is expected in an unfinished game, we still discovered and were told about new issues, that we’re now working on. Some of these will be addressed for the next beta, while others will be fixed closer to launch later this year.
[*][b]Some players seemed to miss the fact that you can take control of your AI team mate[/b], keeping the action entirely in your own hands. We’ll be looking at ways to ensure that this is more clear, so everyone knows that you can either switch characters manually during the match, or set it up to change character automatically to whoever has the ball.
[*][b]The Sentry Shield quickly became “meta”[/b] and everyone picked it, because of some of the unintended ways it could used…[/list]
The above is just a small part of the feedback we received during the beta and we want to thank our players once again for taking part and for sharing your thoughts. This is what will ultimately help us create an even better game that we can all enjoy both during the betas as well as at launch later this year! 

[h1]So, what's next?[/h1]
Firstly, [b]the team is currently hard at work on preparing our next PC beta[/b], which we'll be talking a lot more about in the weeks to come. For now [url=https://www.hyperbrawl.com/newsletter]we recommend signing up to our newsletter[/url] or [url=https://twitter.com/HyperBrawl]following us on Twitter[/url] (or maybe both!), so you'll know as soon as we've got beta details ready to share!

Secondly, we're looking into ways to bring more HyperBrawl to your screens! And no, we're not making a movie, but [b]we may have ordered some livestreaming equipment[/b]... Stay tuned for more on that!

Finally, [b]keep your eyes peeled for our second Behind the Brawl dev blog where we will be diving into weapon design and development[/b], while taking a look at how we may adjust the Sentry Shield so it isn’t quite as overpowered at launch. Here’s a sneak peak…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27827094/484ce1d4af051e9e4a52d23045445e0668f9495d.jpg[/img]

Looking forward to more [b]HyperBrawl[/b]? Be sure to [b]WISHLIST here on Steam[/b] so you never miss a beat. It really helps in making sure that more brawlers discover the game and gives us more poor souls to take down on our way to the top of the leaderboards! [i]*Evil laughter*[/i]

[h2][b]Closed Beta FAQ[/b][/h2]
[b]Where can I play the HyperBrawl Tournament closed beta?[/b]
The closed beta is available on Steam. Keys are available exclusively from Alienware Arena.

[b]When is the closed beta?[/b]
The closed beta runs from March 7th 08:00 GMT / 00:00 PST to March 9th 08:00 GMT / 00:00 PST. The game can only be played during this period.

[b]What’s included in the closed beta?[/b]
[b]4 Heroes[/b]; Shade, Tristan, Toro and Bazooki.
[b]2 Arenas[/b]; Court of Azdritch and Odeon of Talhaca.
[b]4 Weapons[/b]; Hammer, Mag Glove, Grapple and Shield.
[b]4 Game Modes[/b]; Quick Play, Blitz, The Trials and Advanced Tutorial.

[b]Can I play online against other players?[/b]
Yes! We’ve included the Blitz mode in the closed beta to allow you to take on the world and become the HyperBrawl Champion!

[b]Can I play the closed beta offline?[/b]
Yes, The Trials, Advanced Tutorial and Quick Play are all available offline. [b]Please note[/b]: You need to be connected to the internet when booting up the game to be able to access any of the content. Should you go offline for any reason during gameplay, however, you will be able to continue playing offline without issue – at least until you restart the game. 

[b]Can I set up a game with my friends?[/b]
The closed beta doesn’t include the full game, so while you will be able to set up games specifically with your friends in the full game, the closed beta only allows matchmaking when playing online. You can, however, enjoy Quick Play offline with up to 3 friends!

[b]Is there any cross-platform play with the Apple Arcade version?[/b]
No, we’re keeping the versions separate so we can ensure a fair, fun and level playing field on each platform.

[b]Can I talk about and share content from the closed beta?[/b]
You certainly can! There’s no NDA (Non-Disclosure Agreement) in place, which means you’re free to share screenshots, videos, livestreams, blog posts and any and all thoughts and feedback about the closed beta anywhere you want -  and we would love it if you did!

[b]Where should I share my closed beta feedback?[/b]
You’re free to discuss your closed beta experiences anywhere you like, but if you’re looking to give us direct feedback to help us improve the game further, please share this with us on any of our official channels – like right here on Steam!

[b]I didn’t get a key before the beta started; am I out of luck?[/b]
As long as the beta hasn’t ended and all keys haven’t been claimed on Alienware Arena, there’s still time!

[b]Will there be additional betas prior to launch?[/b]
Definitely! We’ve got a few more betas planned for the lead up to launch, so if you didn’t manage to get a key or were unable to play during the beta period, keep an eye on our channels for information about future betas!

notes.title: IMPORTANT MESSAGE ABOUT HYPERBRAWL TOURNAMENT
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27827094/f7fd89cf5094e77d33f00ed4cb036bfcf5f0cd1d.jpg[/img]

[b]HYPEBRAWL TOURNAMENT WILL RELEASE IN EARLY 2019[/b]

We’ve been working hard on HyperBrawl Tournament to make it everything we, and you, want it to be; and your feedback has been invaluable in this process. However, this has meant that our ambitions for the game are bigger than ever, and we have taken the decision that to meet these goals we need to delay the launch of the game on Steam until early 2019. This means that the game will no longer enter Steam’s Early Access program. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27827094/4a203b48e23ca650dcc4923f1deb3ce67f7955da.jpg[/img]

[b]BUT WHY?[/b]

We’ve made this choice because we want the official launch of the game to provide the best possible experience from the very moment you enter the HyperBrawl universe.  In the last twelve months we’ve had amazing feedback from Beta tests, from the multitude of events we’ve attended, from influencers, journalists and esports organisations as well as platform partners. The majority of this was positive, from press accolades to ‘Best in Show’ awards, and we are now so driven to make HyperBrawl Tournament as brilliant as it can be.  

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27827094/878d06fe2bb8c8f0f3e6edd91c45b2f2086bd0f4.jpg[/img]

[b]WE NEED YOUR FEEDBACK[/b]

We would love to get your feedback on the game, and if you haven’t done already please head to the HyperBrawl Tournament website and get your hands on our closed Beta keys. PLUS, feel free to pass the invitation on to friends and family – https://www.hyperbrawl.com/ 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27827094/01e8957e87841c6a78e5db47c9408772e1598614.jpg[/img]

[b]FAQ[/b]

[b]Why have you decided NOT to launch into Early Access?[/b]

Our original Plan was to launch on Steam EA. We’ve done 12 events in 12 months, showcasing the game and built a great community of fans. After discussing the game at length with the community we wanted to give players the best possible game at launch. This meant we had to pursue a full launch initiative whereby we could guarantee users that there would be an active player base. We hope the followers of the project can sympathise with how difficult a decision like this was, and continue to support us in closed Betas and give us valuable feedback on social media. 

[b]Why has the game now got a 2019 release date?[/b]

We’ve had some amazing reactions to the game this year and our ambitions are bigger than ever.  We want to make sure that we live up to those ambitions and build a game that we and the community are proud of. This means we need to invest more time and energy making this game the best it can be at launch; therefore we have moved our release date. We can’t be precise what this date will be, but we will do our best to give the community plenty of notice. 

[b]When will the game be released?[/b]

We have no exact date at present. We want to manage expectations and we’re confident that an early 2019 release window will be achievable. We will give the community as much notice as possible. 

[b]When can you try the game?[/b]

We still plan on having several closed beta tests leading up to launch. In any development process, testing and getting valuable community feedback is paramount. Recently we’ve been working hard on things like gameplay, including player vs player combat and weapon usage; amongst many other things. Art, UI and general game aesthetics are also being developed. We’ve also been busy designing new characters and arenas to ensure there’s plenty of content at launch. If you’re interested in helping us play test builds of the game, or getting involved in closed betas then please sign up via our web site here: https://www.hyperbrawl.com/

We value all constructive feedback and need the communities help in making this game the best it can be.  

[b]How can you help?[/b]

If you’re interested in play testing builds of the game, please sign up via: https://www.hyperbrawl.com/

Also, you can stay up to date with the latest developments via twitter and Instagram here:

Twitter: https://twitter.com/HyperBrawl

Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/hyperbrawl/?hl=en

notes.title: HyperBrawl at Insomnia 60
notes.notes:
We have just returned from Insomnia 60 where we showed our latest build of HyperBrawl Tournament. The game has received an overwhelmingly positive reception everywhere we have taken it so far, with Insomnia offering the most fun and engaging experience yet. 

Once again, the game has proven to be a fun, exciting and competitive experience amongst all age groups and we have witnessed some incredible matches throughout the 4 days. Players have started to master the mechanics and some even developing their own tactics and strategies far beyond our comprehension. 

There’s been a great deal of laughs, shouts, screams, high fives, and we feel as though we’re achieving our goal in making such a positive and enjoyable experience for as many people as possible.

Thank you to everyone that came by and checked the game out! We’d like to give a special shout out to Tom and Ben who spent the best part of 3 days at the stand mastering the game and eventually beating us developers!

We have gained a great amount of feedback and inspiration from everyone and we’re excited to be back in the studio working on making the best game we possibly can! 

Keep in touch as we have some awesome stuff to share with you, and we can’t wait to play some more HyperBrawl with you soon!

notes.title: HyperBrawl Tournament at EGX Rezzed 2017
notes.notes:
We have just returned from EGX Rezzed in London after HyperBrawl’s first public outing in the UK. After 3 days and hundreds of intense games we can say the game was hugely successful. 
We’ve witnessed some incredible moments, superb goals, chaotic brawls, phenomenal sudden death rounds, unbelievable come backs and much more.

The game has proven to be incredibly fun amongst fighting game fans, sports game fans, older gamers, younger gamers, families, and everyone in between. It has been received far better than we imagined, with players coming up with new tactics, strategies, and ideas far beyond our imagination. We’re ashamed to say us developers were even beaten by new players on several occasions.   
  
Here's a couple of quotes from some of the people who played - 

[i]“@HyperBrawl big highlight from #Rezzed today. Great tense multiplayer fun”

”Definitely think @HyperBrawl was one of the standouts, incredibly fun game and the devs are super nice guys”[/i]

We’ve gained lots of feedback from our time at EGX Rezzed, we have lots of exciting new content to add to the game and we can’t wait to play some more HyperBrawl with you in the near future! 

To conclude here’s a short clip of just one of the awesome moments we had at the event - [url]https://youtu.be/99gZefdQL0c[/url]
